Take a boat onto the lower Zambezi with tigerfish in mind. Spend a Zambian river day focused on your casts and the next strike.

KEY FACTS

A Zambia Tourism account describes September–November as a favorable Lower Zambezi reference, with warming, clearer conditions before the rains. It discusses fishing around current features and notes hippos and crocodiles. The article dates to 2020.

SEASON

When this trip makes sense.

The September–November reference is historical seasonal guidance, not a current river or catch report. Confirm the selected reach and conditions with the operator. Do not extend this window to every African river or every species called tigerfish.

Historical seasonal guidance from 2020.

Zambia Tourism — Lower Zambezi tiger fishing ↗

Keep access boat-led

This guide does not recommend independent bank access or wading. Ask the operator how anglers board, fish and move between locations, and follow its wildlife-aware arrangements. Do not infer safety from a photograph of calm water. A fishing plan here must include the way you reaches and uses the river, not just the rods in the bag.

Resolve the whole terminal system

Have the operator specify the intended presentation, bite protection, connections, hooks and rod-and-line match. Do not copy a trout leader onto this trip. Avoid a universal numeric leader recommendation without the exact method and materials. Have a spare system prepared in the same configuration rather than carrying unrelated pieces that may not work together.

Compare the actual fishing package

Ask which days are dedicated to fishing versus other activities, what tackle is supplied and how the boat is shared. An appealing safari package does not necessarily mean full fishing days. Keep sun coverage, rain protection and dry storage compact. Request a short list of locally useful replacements and tools before adding heavy or specialized items.

LICENCE & PERMITS

Fishing licence for Zambia
